summary: The shot's opening has a big pop: he is standing with the blade at his chest at 36.59, then lunges into a bent-over, head-down pose with the arm overhead by 36.63-36.66, with no anticipation. The later frames settle into a held reach, and the blade stays in his hand.

faults.what: Between 36.59 and 36.63 the torso and head jump from upright, relaxed standing to a deep lean with the head tilted down and the body shifted and cropped low in frame. This is a snap with no in-between frames. By 36.66 the arm is straight overhead with the blade pointing up.
faults.fix: Add 4-6 frames of in-between motion, or cut on the lean pose. Alternatively start the shot on the raised-blade pose.

faults.what: There is no anticipation or hip lead before the big move. He goes from a casual stance to the overhead raise in about 1/30 s. This clashes with the quiet 'stops being funny' feel.
faults.fix: Retime the move slower, with a small dip or wind-up. Alternatively remove the raise and start on the held pose.

faults.what: The measured spike at 36.867. At 36.86-36.90 the body and head are still leaned over, then by 36.93 the torso straightens quickly and the head rises. This looks like a fast snap rather than an eased move.
faults.fix: Smooth the torso and head rise over a few more frames, with overshoot and settle.

faults.what: At 36.63-36.73 the head sits at the bottom of the frame and the raised blade tip nearly touches or leaves the top edge. The framing is awkward for a quiet beat.
faults.fix: Reframe or lower the framing offset so the head and the blade tip both stay in frame.

faults.what: The held pose is a stiff arm straight across the chest with the blade pointing up behind it. It is flat and reads as a plain bar with little line of action. The face is nearly blank and static from 36.96 to 37.10.
faults.fix: Raise the blade into a clearer silhouette, add a head tilt or an expression change, and give the hand a firmer grip.
